notes: Tested: a custom auth config created without `oauth_redirect_uri` sends `https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add`. Register exactly the URI your auth config sends, or set `oauth_redirect_uri` to `https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback` and register that instead.
Composio supports two toolkits: **Slack** (user-level auth) and **Slackbot** (bot-level auth).
Composio defaults the redirect URI to `https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add` unless overridden.
Data handled via Composio is encrypted and subject to a 30-day retention policy.

assumption: An agent that interacts with any user's Slack workspace across channels, messages, and files using distributed OAuth.

verdict.headline: Slack offers instant self-serve app creation for private use, but public distribution and Marketplace publishing require strict reviews and active workspace prerequisites.
verdict.summary: Developers can create an app instantly via the Slack API portal and test via OAuth. However, unlisted apps face strict rate limits and workspace restrictions, while public Marketplace publishing requires an extensive review process taking up to 10 weeks and 10 active workspaces.

handsOnEffort.label: 4–8 hours
handsOnEffort.basis: Configuring app credentials, setting up OAuth redirect flows, and implementing scopes.

timeToFirstConnection.label: 1 hour
timeToFirstConnection.basis: Instant self-serve app creation at api.slack.com/apps.

timeToProduction.label: 10–12 weeks
timeToProduction.basis: Slack Marketplace preliminary review takes up to 10 business days and functional review takes up to 10 weeks.

verdict.longestPole: Slack Marketplace functional review process (up to 10 weeks)
verdict.costDetail: Developing and submitting apps to Slack is free; API access and standard tiers carry no direct developer fee.

easierPaths.effect: Bypasses the Slack Marketplace review entirely, allowing immediate deployment via installation URLs.

factors.detail: Developers can instantly register apps via the Slack API portal.
Submitting to the Slack Marketplace requires a preliminary and functional review.
Basic app creation and unlisted distribution do not mandate formal business verification.
No mandatory third-party security audit is required for basic Marketplace apps, though compliance requirements apply.
Slack API access is included with workspace plans without separate developer subscription fees.
No partner program is required to build and distribute standard Slack integrations.
Marketplace submission requires the app to already be installed and active on 10 or more workspaces.
Standard OAuth flow handles per-workspace authorization automatically.

phases.title: Register your Slack app
phases.outcome: An unconfigured Slack application object inside your developer account.

steps.title: Create a new Slack app
steps.details: Go to the [Slack API Apps portal](https://api.slack.com/apps) [P4, S15], click **Create New App**, choose **From scratch**, enter your app name and select your development workspace.
steps.agentAssist: Draft a name and select target scopes based on your integration use case.

phases.title: Configure OAuth credentials and redirect URIs
phases.outcome: Configured Client ID, Client Secret, and valid OAuth redirect URLs.

steps.title: Set up redirect URLs
steps.details: In your app dashboard, navigate to **OAuth & Permissions** in the sidebar. Under **Redirect URLs**, click **Add New Redirect URL** and enter `https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add` [P2, S1]. Click **Save URLs**.
steps.agentAssist: Prepare the correct Composio callback URLs to paste into the Slack console.

steps.title: Add required OAuth scopes
steps.details: On the same **OAuth & Permissions** page, scroll down to **Scopes**. Under **User Token Scopes** or **Bot Token Scopes**, click **Add an OAuth Scope** and add your required permissions (e.g., `channels:read`, `chat:write`) [P1, S1].
steps.agentAssist: Review your agent requirements and compile the exact list of scopes needed.

phases.title: Test authentication with your own account
phases.outcome: Verified OAuth authorization code grant flow against your development workspace.

steps.title: Activate public distribution for testing
steps.details: Navigate to **Manage Distribution** in the sidebar and click **Activate Public Distribution** [S15]. This allows you to generate installation URLs for OAuth testing.
steps.agentAssist: Check configuration settings to ensure distribution requirements are met.

steps.title: Perform test installation flow
steps.details: Copy your **Client ID** and **Client Secret** from **Basic Information**. Initiate an authorization request to `https://slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize` with your client_id, scopes, and redirect_uri to test token exchange via `https://slack.com/api/oauth.v2.access` [S1, S2].
steps.agentAssist: Write a test script to automate token exchange verification against Slack's OAuth endpoints.

phases.title: Prepare for Slack Marketplace review (Optional)
phases.outcome: An app ready for public submission with 10+ active workspaces.

steps.title: Accumulate active workspace installs
steps.details: Distribute your app via installation links and ensure it is installed and used on 10 or more active workspaces in the past 28 days before applying for Marketplace listing [S18].
steps.agentAssist: Track installation counts and usage metrics across connected workspaces.

phases.title: Review and wait
phases.outcome: Slack Marketplace approval or preliminary feedback.

steps.title: Submit app to Slack Marketplace
steps.details: Submit your app via the developer portal for Marketplace review. Slack performs a preliminary review taking up to 10 business days, followed by a functional review taking up to 10 weeks [S18].
steps.agentAssist: Gather documentation, privacy policy links, and screen recordings for the submission form.

phases.title: Go live in Composio
phases.outcome: Slack connected as an active custom OAuth toolkit inside Composio.

steps.title: Create custom auth config in Composio
steps.details: Go to your Composio dashboard, navigate to **Custom Auth Settings**, select **Slack**, and provide your Slack App's **Client ID** and **Client Secret** [S9].
steps.agentAssist: Format your Client ID and Client Secret for safe transfer into Composio.

steps.title: Initiate connection session
steps.details: Trigger a connection request via the Composio SDK or API, passing your custom auth config ID so that user authentication redirects correctly through `https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add` [P2, S9].
steps.agentAssist: Write the initialization snippet using Composio client libraries to test the connection flow.

requirements.detail: Required to access api.slack.com/apps and create applications.
Must be configured in app settings to handle authorization callbacks.
Required before submitting an app to the Slack Marketplace.

scopes.purpose: View basic information about public channels in the workspace.
Manage public channels and create new channels.
Send messages on behalf of the authenticated user or bot.
View files shared in channels and private conversations.

blockers.title: This app isn't listed in the Slack Marketplace
blockers.symptom: Users see an installation error message when trying to add your unlisted distributed app to their workspace.
blockers.howToProceed: Disable **Require apps from Slack Marketplace** under the workspace settings at `Settings → Apps & Workflows → App Management Settings`.

blockers.title: Admin approval required during auth
blockers.symptom: Users are blocked from authenticating and prompted to submit a request to their workspace admin.
blockers.howToProceed: Ensure **Require approved apps** is disabled in the workspace app management settings, or have a workspace administrator approve the app installation.

blockers.title: Rate Limit Exceeded (HTTP 429)
blockers.symptom: API requests fail with status 429 and a Retry-After header.
blockers.howToProceed: Respect the Retry-After header value returned by Slack and implement exponential backoff. Adhere to method-specific rate limits (Tiers 1–4 and special caps like 1 msg/sec for chat.postMessage).

nuances.title: Token Rotation & Lifetimes
nuances.detail: Slack tokens may use token rotation depending on configuration. Access tokens and refresh tokens follow specific rotation guidelines provided in Slack's developer documentation.

nuances.title: PKCE Support
nuances.detail: Slack supports PKCE (Proof Key for Code Exchange) using S256 hashing for public clients and authorization code flows.

nuances.title: Rate Limits and Tiers
nuances.detail: Slack API rate limits apply per method per app per workspace across Tiers 1 through 4, alongside special limits and non-Marketplace restrictions.

steps: Navigate to the Composio dashboard and open custom OAuth settings for Slack.
Paste your Slack App's Client ID and Client Secret into the Composio configuration fields.
Verify that the redirect URI points to `https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add`.
Initiate an authentication session via Composio using your custom auth config ID.
